questions.problem:
The triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dx\,dy\,dz
$$

is defined over the type II region $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-8\le y\le {sin}^{2}⁡z,\,0\le z\le \pi ,\,-2y-1\le x\le {y}^{2}+2z}.
$$

What is $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
A type II region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(y,z)\le x\le {u}_{2}(y,z)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type II region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/a905e1f60fb0aa865c071fcbccbfecb30dcac7a74b4b647d24a40f4c89ff1935.png)

 

If $R$ is a type II region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(y,z)=-2y-1,\,{u}_{2}(y,z)={y}^{2}+2z.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2y-1}^{{y}^{2}+2z}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA.
$$

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-8\le y\le {sin}^{2}⁡z,\,0\le z\le \pi }.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2y-1}^{{y}^{2}+2z}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{-8}^{{sin}^{2}⁡z}[{\int }_{-2y-1}^{{y}^{2}+2z}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dy\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{-8}^{{sin}^{2}⁡z}{\int }_{-2y-1}^{{y}^{2}+2z}f(x,y,z)\,dx\,dy\,dz.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=0+\pi =\pi .
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y}12z\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le 4-{y}^{2}}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y}12z\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}12z[x]_{x=0}^{x=y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}12z(y-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}12yz\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}yz\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-{y}^{2}}12yz\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}6y[{z}^{2}]_{z=0}^{z=4-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}6y(4-{y}^{2})^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(96y-48{y}^{3}+6{y}^{5})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[48{y}^{2}-12{y}^{4}+{y}^{6}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =48(2)^{2}-12(2)^{4}+(2)^{6} \\  & =64\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y+2z}2\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,0\le z\le 2y}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y+2z}2\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}2[x]_{x=0}^{x=y+2z}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2(y+2z-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2y+4z\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2y+4z\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2y}2y+4z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[2yz+2{z}^{2}]_{z=0}^{z=2y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2y(2y)+2(2y)^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}4{y}^{2}+8{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}12{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[4{y}^{3}]_{y=1}^{y=3} \\  & =4(27-1) \\  & =104\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z}4xz\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{4-2y}}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z}4xz\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}[2z{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=z}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2z({z}^{2}-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{z}^{3}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2{z}^{3}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2y}}2{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=\sqrt{4-2y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{4-2y)})^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(4-2y)^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(16-16y+4{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}8-8y+2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[8y-4{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =16-16+\frac{16}{3} \\  & =\frac{16}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2z}}\frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,y\le z\le y+1}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2z}}\frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{4}[{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{2z}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{4}(2z-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{2}z\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{1}{2}z\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{y}^{y+1}\frac{1}{2}z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{4}[{z}^{2}]_{z=y}^{z=y+1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{4}((y+1)^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{4}(2y+1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[{y}^{2}+y]}_{y=1}^{y=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(9+3)-\frac{1}{4}(1+1) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}2+2{e}^{x}\,\text{d}V
$$

where $R$ is the type II region given by 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,0\le z\le 1,\,-z\le x\le 0}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2+2{e}^{x}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-z}^{0}2+2{e}^{x}\,dx\,dz\,dy.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-z}^{0}2+2{e}^{x}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{-z}^{0}2+2{e}^{x}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}[2x+2{e}^{x}]_{x=-z}^{x=0}dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}0+2{e}^{0}-2(-z)-2{e}^{-z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}2+2z-2{e}^{-z}\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}2+2z-2{e}^{-z}\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[{\int }_{0}^{1}2+2z-2{e}^{-z}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{[2z+{z}^{2}+2{e}^{-z}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(2+1+2{e}^{-1})-2{e}^{0}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}1+2{e}^{-1}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}1+2{e}^{-1}\,dy & =(1+2{e}^{-1})[y]_{y=-1}^{y=0} \\  & =(1+2{e}^{-1})(0-(-1)) \\  & =2{e}^{-1}+1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:

$$

where the region $R$ is given by

and $D$ is a finite region in $yz$-plane enclosed between the $y$-axis, the line $y=1$ and the parabola $z=-{y}^{2}$ in the fourth quadrant.

Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+1}dx]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+1}dx]dA & ={∬}_{D}[x]_{x=0}^{x={y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+1}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+1\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate the double integral above over the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/38ea49a6fae41574107b2ba68a578586a306cf43d419d4de5699dcfa009137c2.png)

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+1\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}}^{0}{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+1\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{-{y}^{2}}^{0}{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}+1\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[({y}^{2}+1)z+\frac{1}{3}{z}^{3}]}_{z=-{y}^{2}}^{z=0}dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}+1)((0-(-{y}^{2}))+\frac{1}{3}(0-{(-{y}^{2})}^{3})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}+1){y}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{y}^{6}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{4}+{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{y}^{6}\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{1}{5}{y}^{5}+\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}+\frac{1}{21}{y}^{7}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{21} \\  & =\frac{61}{105}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z\sqrt{3}}2y\,dx]dA & ={∬}_{D}2y[x]_{x=0}^{x=z\sqrt{3}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}2yz\sqrt{3}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$

For a type II region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type II region enclosed between the back surface $x={u}_{1}(y,z)=1$ and the front surface $x={u}_{2}(y,z)=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/6cc327f63d7141c43852e868812a7cff1ec9ae0acfed636ff896ceb204b6fbf0.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,1\le x\le 2}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I *plane* region in the $yz$-plane with the upper curve

$$
(y-1)^{2}+{z}^{2}=1\,⟺\,z=\sqrt{1-(y-1)^{2}}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/a0fb19d32c2545e5c2a61cbb54536e7c28b1a54dbce51c7752c3687035d6c3d6.png)

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-(y-1)^{2}}}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-(y-1)^{2}}}[{x}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-(y-1)^{2}}}3\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the missing limits in the repeated integral below

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V
= 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y
$$

where $R$ is the type II region defined as

$$
R=\left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq y \leq 4, \: -y^2 \leq z \leq \sqrt{y}, \: -2 \leq x \leq ye^{z+2} \right\}.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
A type II region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z)  \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \: u_1(y,z) \leq x \leq u_2(y,z) \big\}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type II region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/1b49704bf6d5837a18d8b5dbb8b420d430d5e3881507540fb62a45cf1f6ce52f.png)

 

If $R$ is a type II region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm{d}x \right]\,\textrm d A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
u_1(y,z) = -2, \qquad u_2(y,z)  = ye^{z+2}.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{-2}^{ye^{z+2}} f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}x \right] \mathrm{d}A.
$$

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D =\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq y \leq 4, \: -y^2 \leq z \leq \sqrt{y} \right\}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2}^{y{e}^{z+2}}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}}^{\sqrt{y}}[{\int }_{-2}^{y{e}^{z+2}}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dz\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}}^{\sqrt{y}}{\int }_{-2}^{y{e}^{z+2}}f(x,y,z)\,dx\,dz\,dy.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}[x]_{x=0}^{x=z}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}(z-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{z\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{z\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}{\int }_{0}^{2\sqrt{1-y}}\frac{z\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}{[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=2\sqrt{1-y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}(\frac{4(1-y)}{2}-0)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =[\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)]_{y=0}^{y=\pi /6} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type II Region
canonical_examples.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 4x^3  \: \mathrm{d}V
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \: 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{y} \right\},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $yz$-plane enclosed between the $y$-axis, the $z$-axis, and the line $z = 4-y$ in the first quadrant.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} 4x^3 \, \textrm{d}V
= 
\iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{y}} 4x^3 \, \mathrm{d}x \right] \mathrm{d}A.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}4{x}^{3}\,dx]dA & ={∬}_{D}[{x}^{4}]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{y}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}{(\sqrt{y})}^{4}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/3c8712fa0a30ad94f503efe5e080ee89f83eb21f19fba45033bbedeab08ac816.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{4-y}{y}^{2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[{\int }_{0}^{4-y}{y}^{2}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[{y}^{2}z]_{z=0}^{z=4-y}dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{y}^{2}(4-y)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}4{y}^{2}-{y}^{3}\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=4} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}(64-0)-\frac{1}{4}(256-0) \\  & =\frac{64}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type II Region Given a Diagram
canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/fc19dd4415663ab027e0fc386d4c5bc81a28c1bc26d5f6cf2083f4f4228a4dea.png)

 

Evaluate the triple integral 
$\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 12z^2 \: \mathrm{d}V$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/f25c393f10c35ffd9b4fa91cdf672a516cf6cff974a8aa563d350619a64b79bd.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 3-y-z \big\},
$$

where

$$
D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1 \big\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/145f0d494ffe24de84e3a289b3a7316d3f4933f193d734aed118609f7fb9f94f.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 3-y-z \big\}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
\iiint \limits_{R}  12z^2  \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{3-y-z}  12z^2  \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3-y-z}12{z}^{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{3-y-z}12{z}^{2}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}12{z}^{2}[x]_{x=0}^{x=3-y-z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}12{z}^{2}(3-y-z)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(36{z}^{2}-12y{z}^{2}-12{z}^{3})\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(36{z}^{2}-12y{z}^{2}-12{z}^{3})\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(36{z}^{2}-12y{z}^{2}-12{z}^{3})\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[12{z}^{3}-4y{z}^{3}-3{z}^{4}]_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(12-4y-3)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(9-4y)\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(9-4y)\,dy & =[9y-2{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =(9-2)-0 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$
